name: Warrior
tagline: The baseline tank: no self-heals, rage economy, unmatched group demand.
summary: Warriors define Classic tanking and remain the default main tank for a reason: threat, mitigation, and cooldowns all scale with gear. The trade-off is a slow, resource-hungry solo start. If you want to be the person every dungeon group needs, this is it.
leveling: Expect the slowest first 20 levels. Pull one mob at a time, bandage between fights, and buy a weapon upgrade before anything else. Your damage is your weapon.
dualSpec: Protection for dungeon runs and raids, Fury for solo and farming. Swap only after 40 when the second spec unlocks.
tips: Train First Aid early — bandages are your only sustain.
Weapon skill matters more than raw stats while leveling.
Learn to pull two mobs safely; rage generation rewards controlled multi-pulls.

name: Paladin
tagline: Durable melee healer with the best group blessings and a forgiving solo path.
summary: Paladins trade burst for reliability: plate, shields, and self-healing make them hard to kill. Healing is the safest group role, and Retribution levels comfortably. Whether protection tanking is viable depends on the build — verify in game before committing.
leveling: Seal-and-judge rotation with auto-attacks, plus self-heals, makes solo leveling steady rather than fast. Consecration smooths multi-pulls once available.
dualSpec: Holy for groups, Retribution for solo and PvP. Protection only if you have confirmed a working tank build.
tips: Keep Blessing of Might on melee and Wisdom on casters.
Divine Shield is your reset button — use it before you need it.
Save Lay on Hands for genuine emergencies.

name: Hunter
tagline: Fastest solo leveler in the game: your pet tanks, you kite.
summary: Hunters level faster than anything else because the pet absorbs damage and you control the fight from range. The skill ceiling moves to pet management, ammo economy, and kiting — all of which matter more in Forever's denser launch-week zones.
leveling: Send the pet in, keep it fed, and use a weapon that matches your level. Track your pet's happiness — an unhappy pet does less damage and may abandon you.
dualSpec: Beast Mastery for solo leveling and farming, Marksmanship for raid single-target. Survival is a PvP pick.
tips: Feed your pet before long sessions; it is not optional.
Carry two ammo stacks — launch-week vendors run dry.
Learn to kite elites; it turns impossible pulls into XP.

name: Rogue
tagline: Stealth, lockpicking, and the best single-target melee toolkit.
summary: Rogues bring control and strong single-target damage but pay for it with thin defenses. Stealth changes how you approach quests and dungeons, and lockpicking opens shortcuts and lockboxes that many groups will pay for.
leveling: Stealth past what you cannot fight, sap casters, and use Vanish as an escape. Weapon skill and poison supply are your main chores.
dualSpec: Combat swords for PvE damage, Subtlety for PvP. Level lockpicking alongside so you never lose access.
tips: Pickpocket humanoids constantly — it is free gold.
Keep poisons stocked; they are a large share of your damage.
Sap then pull casters to avoid nasty openers.

name: Priest
tagline: The best healing toolkit and a surprisingly smooth wand-based solo path.
summary: Priests are the most complete healer: shields, renews, dispels, and resurrection. Solo leveling is better than its reputation thanks to wand damage and Spirit Tap, which turns kills into mana.
leveling: Wand-plus-Spirit-Tap is the classic low-friction path. Shadow is more engaging but wants hit gear before it feels good.
dualSpec: Holy or Discipline for groups, Shadow for solo and PvP. Healers are always in demand — you will never wait for a group.
tips: Buy the best wand you can afford at every level bracket.
Dispel magic in dungeons; it saves more runs than raw healing.
Spirit Tap makes killing faster than drinking.

name: Shaman
tagline: Totem support and burst damage; the Horde's best utility pick.
summary: Shamans bring group-wide totems, strong burst, and a healing toolkit that keeps groups alive through messy pulls. Totem placement is the real skill — a well-placed Earthbind or Grounding Totem wins fights before they start.
leveling: Weapon imbues carry your damage early; Earthbind Totem makes kiting elites realistic. Mana is the limiting factor, so plan pulls around it.
dualSpec: Restoration for groups, Enhancement for solo and PvP. Elemental is the PvP burst pick.
tips: Totem macros are mandatory for group content.
Drop Grounding Totem before pulling casters.
Keep water totems down for the whole group, not just yourself.

name: Mage
tagline: Portals, conjured food, and the best AoE farming in the game.
summary: Mages are the convenience class: free food and water, portals to every capital, and frost control that makes solo play safe. AoE farming turns them into gold machines — but launch-week farming spots will be contested.
leveling: Frost is the safe solo spec: slows, blocks, and efficient AoE once you have the toolkit. Fire is a later, group-oriented pick.
dualSpec: Frost for AoE farming and solo, Fire for single-target raid damage. Swap after 40 when the second spec arrives.
tips: Conjure water before every pull; mana is your clock.
Blink through walls of mobs to reset fights safely.
Have a backup farming spot for launch week.

name: Warlock
tagline: Pet sustain, self-resources, and a free mount at 40.
summary: Warlocks level with almost no downtime: the Voidwalker tanks, Drain Life sustains, and healthstones keep you alive. Fear is both a tool and a liability — learn where it causes patrols to bring friends.
leveling: Voidwalker plus DoT-and-drain is the safest path. Fear-juggling speeds things up but can pull extra mobs; use it deliberately.
dualSpec: Affliction for solo and farming, Demonology or Destruction for groups. The free mount at 40 is a real gold swing.
tips: Carry soul shards for summons and healthstones.
Curse of Agony on everything, then drain.
Do not fear near patrol paths.

name: Druid
tagline: The most flexible class: bear tank, cat DPS, or tree healer in one character.
summary: Druids can fill any group role, which makes them the best class for players who hate being locked out of content. The catch is gear competition: feral and caster gear rarely overlap, so plan your loot early.
leveling: Cat form kills fast with no mana downtime; bear form handles elites. You will rarely need to drink.
dualSpec: Feral covers tanking and melee DPS in one spec; Restoration for healing. Decide your main role before gearing.
tips: Bear form is a real tank — do not be shy about tanking dungeons.
Keep both feral and caster gear sets as you level.
Innervate your healer, not yourself.
